Pool service in Sun City, AZ usually means keeping a private backyard pool clean, balanced and safe to step into, sometimes for owners who are not home all year. This page is about those home pools, not the community recreation pools. It covers the local water, care while you travel, how to keep pool chores safe, and how to reach a pool company that works locally without paying for the call.

Phoenix Pool Cleaning Pro is a free phone line, not a pool company. Phone (623) 240-0428 and a recorded assistant asks you to sum up the pool trouble in a sentence or two, then transfers the call to an independent, locally owned pool service company. That company visits, quotes and does the work, and you pay it directly.

Sun City: private pools with their own needs

Sun City is an unincorporated community in Maricopa County, so it has no city hall of its own. It opened in 1960 as a retirement community, and county zoning places it in a Senior Citizens overlay that requires at least one person 55 or older in each home. It has community pools, but a pool behind your own house is a different matter. A private pool is your responsibility from the water to the equipment pad. In the Valley's heat, that means steady chlorine, regular brushing and a pump that runs every day, even when no one is swimming.

Water comes from EPCOR, which runs the Sun City water system (state system number AZ0407099) and publishes a water quality report for it every year. The 2025 report puts hardness at 7 to 11 grains per gallon, which counts as hard water, and EPCOR says it does not treat the water for hardness. Hard water leaves calcium scale on tile and inside heaters and salt cells, and because pools lose water to evaporation and get topped off, the minerals add up over time.

Services Sun City pool owners ask about

Regular pool cleaning and weekly maintenance covers most needs, and it matters most when you are away and cannot see the water. A pool that turned green during a missed week calls for green pool cleanup. A heater that warms the water for cooler months is covered under pool heater repair, and a filter that has gone months without attention is the subject of pool filter cleaning.

Pool care while you are away

If you spend part of the year somewhere else, the pool keeps running without you. A few arrangements before you leave save a lot of trouble when you get back.

Keep weekly service going

Heat and sun burn off chlorine quickly, and a pool can turn green between visits. Ask for a steady weekly schedule rather than pausing service while you travel.

Sort out gate access

Decide how the pool company gets into the yard, who else has a key, and that the gate latches behind every visit. A gate left open is a safety risk for any child nearby.

Agree on what to do about problems

Tell the company how to reach you, and set a dollar amount it may spend on a repair without calling first. Anything above that waits for your approval.

Pool service in Sun City, AZ: keeping pool chores safe

Some pool jobs are easy to hand off, and handing them off is often the safer choice. Lifting heavy chemical jugs, leaning out over the water with a long pole and working on a hot deck in summer are where falls, strains and heat illness happen. A pool service company can carry that load, and these habits help for anything you still do.

  • Work early or late. Do any pool chore in the cool of the morning or evening, drink water and stop if you feel dizzy or overheated.
  • Watch your footing. Wet decks and pool steps get slick. A handrail at the steps and nonslip surfaces help.
  • Leave the heavy lifting. Let the pool company carry and handle chemical containers.
  • Never mix pool chemicals with each other. Store them apart, dry, shaded and out of reach of visiting grandchildren, and follow the label.
  • Plan for young visitors. Never leave a child unsupervised near the water. Keep gates latched and doors to the pool area closed, and consider a pool alarm or safety cover.

Safe checks before you call

  • Look at the water. Cloudy or green water, or a bottom you cannot see, means stay out and keep others out.
  • Check the baskets from the deck. Empty the skimmer basket if you can reach it easily.
  • Read the filter gauge. Write down the number and share it on the call.
  • Check the timer. Confirm the pump is set to run, especially after a power outage.

Smell gas near a pool heater? Leave the area. Do not touch the heater or any switch. From a safe distance, call 911 or the gas company named on your bill.

Check the license first. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) licenses contractors, and its residential classifications include R-6, Swimming Pool Service and Repair. Repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a licensed contractor; whether a cleaning-only service needs a license is not spelled out, so ask the ROC if it matters to you. Ask the company for its ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search (opens in a new tab) before work begins. The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Who can service my pool in Sun City, AZ?

Call the free line, day or night. A recorded assistant takes down what the backyard pool is doing, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned pool service company that works in Sun City. That company quotes, does the work and bills you directly. When nobody there can pick up, your details reach the company so it can ring you.

Who provides electricity to Sun City, AZ?

Your electric bill names your utility, and that is the company to call about an outage or a downed line. If the lights work but the pool pump will not run, the problem is at the pool equipment or its circuit, which is a job for a pool company or an electrician, not the utility. Reset a tripped pool breaker once, and if it trips again, leave it off and call.

Who provides water in Sun City, AZ?

EPCOR runs the Sun City water system and publishes a yearly water quality report for it. The report lists where the water comes from and what is in it, including hardness (7 to 11 grains per gallon in the 2025 report), which affects how fast scale builds up on pool tile and equipment.

Can someone look after my pool while I am away for the summer?

Many pool service companies offer regular weekly visits whether or not you are home. Ask the company you are put through to how it handles gate access, what it does if it finds a problem while you are gone, and how it will reach you.

Is this page about the Sun City recreation center pools?

No. The community pools are run by the community, and their hours and rules come from them. This page and the line are for private pools at Sun City homes.
